overview.text: Mele Kyari, former Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, appeared before the Senate Committee on Public Accounts to answer questions over N210 trillion in financial transactions flagged in the company's 2017–2023 accounts.
A former Group Managing Director of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) told lawmakers that ₦210 trillion referenced in an audit report is not missing.
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) recovered $3 million and N1.3 billion in unremitted revenues from two firms.

cards.headline: N210tn audit queries: Kyari finally appears before Senate panel
cards.byline: BusinessDay · Tue 10 Nov, 20:13 Lagos · latest of 3 reports from 3 outlets
cards.what_happened: Mele Kyari, former Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, appeared before the Senate Committee on Public Accounts to answer questions over N210 trillion in financial transactions flagged in the company's 2017–2023 accounts.
key_facts: Mele Kyari appeared before the Senate Committee on Public Accounts on Tuesday.
The N210 trillion comprises N103 trillion accrued expenses and N107 trillion sundry receivables.
The committee is chaired by Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo, representing Gombe North.
Ex-NNPCL boss Kyari appeared before a Senate panel. (The Eagle Online)

analysis: Why it matters: The scale of the unexplained entries, and lawmakers' demands for the identities of counterparties and supporting documentation, bear directly on transparency over public oil-company finances. The outcome will determine whether former management is held accountable for the recorded figures.
named: Office of the Auditor-General for the Federation

cards.headline: NNPC Audit Report: Former GMD tells lawmakers ₦210 trillion isn’t missing
cards.what_happened: A former Group Managing Director of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) told lawmakers that ₦210 trillion referenced in an audit report is not missing. The statement responds to scrutiny of NNPC's audit findings before the National Assembly.
analysis: Why it matters: The dispute over a reported ₦210 trillion gap in NNPC accounts bears directly on the accountability of public oil revenue and the reliability of audit findings on a state-owned company.

cards.headline: EFCC recovers $3m, N1.3bn unremitted revenues from two firms, hands over funds to RMAFC
cards.what_happened: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) recovered $3 million and N1.3 billion in unremitted revenues from two firms. The recovered funds were handed over to the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC).
key_facts: EFCC recovered $3m and N1.3bn in unremitted revenues from two firms.
The recovered funds were handed over to the RMAFC.
analysis: Why it matters: The recovery targets unremitted revenues owed to public finances, showing enforcement against companies that withheld government money.
named: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission

cards.headline: N210trn not missing from NNPC – Mele Kyari tells Senate
cards.what_happened: Former NNPC Group Chief Executive Mele Kyari told the Senate that N210 trillion is not missing from the Nigerian National Petroleum Company. The claim was made in response to allegations about the sum's whereabouts.
key_facts: Mele Kyari told the Senate that N210trn is not missing from NNPC.
analysis: Why it matters: The claim concerns a very large sum linked to Nigeria's national oil company, a public money and transparency matter that depends on the accounting Kyari presented to the Senate.

cards.headline: No N210tn missing from NNPC — Kyari
cards.what_happened: NNPC Limited Group Chief Executive Mele Kyari has denied that N210 trillion went missing from the state oil company, according to a Punch Newspapers report. The headline reflects a rebuttal of allegations concerning the corporation's finances. The article text provided is limited to the headline, so further details of the claims and the response are not available.
